chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Barqi, from Ismail ibn Mihran, from Sulayman al-Ja'fari, from Abu al-Hasan al-Ridha (peace be upon him) who said:
The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: 'The best of your women have five (qualities).' It was said: 'O Commander of the Faithful, and what are the five?'

He said: 'The modest, the gentle, the supportive — the one who, when her husband is angered, does not neglect him even for the blink of an eye until he is pleased; and when her husband is absent from her, she protects him (his interests) during his absence. Thus, that (woman) is a worker from the workers of God, and a worker of God will not fail.'

key_terms.اللينة: Al-Layyina — the soft and tender one; kindness in disposition
key_terms.المؤاتية: Al-Mu'atiya — the cooperative, supportive one; one who aligns with her husband's needs
key_terms.الهينة: Al-Hayyina — the modest, gentle one; someone of easy and calm temperament
key_terms.عمال الله: 'Ummal Allah — the workers/agents of God; those who serve divine purposes through their deeds

ai.seo_question: What are the five qualities of the best wife according to Imam Ali in al-Kafi?
ai.summary: Imam al-Ridha (AS) transmits a teaching of Imam Ali (AS), Commander of the Faithful, outlining five praiseworthy qualities in women: gentleness, softness, and supportiveness, coupled with unwavering patience during marital discord and faithful guardianship of the husband's interests during his absence. The teaching concludes with a powerful theological affirmation — such a woman is counted among the 'workers of God,' a divine agent whose effort will never go unrewarded. This hadith was addressed to the early Muslim community as a model of spousal virtue rooted in patience and loyalty.
